clusterer: Claude Opus 5.5 acting as meaning-equivalence judge (same role an API call plays in pipeline.py). Variants that differ only in wording share a cluster.

lines.note: 'Angioloni' is the augmentative of angelo: it adds size, but also an affectionate, comic deflation of the Apocalypse. Dignified versions lose that irreverence.

clusters.gloss: big / hulking angels (augmentative kept as size, comic)
mighty / towering angels (augmentative turned into grandeur)

lines.note: 'Cantone' is an everyday word for a street corner. Is the Last Judgement staged at the 'four corners of the earth' or on a Roman street?

clusters.gloss: the four corners of the world (biblical, cosmic)
they blow, then call out in a huge voice

lines.note: 'Fora a chi tocca' is a call from games and queues: 'out with whoever's turn it is'. This register choice decides whether the Judgement is a turn-taking game, a waiting room, or Scripture.
'Filastrocca' means a nursery or counting rhyme, and by extension a long string of things. Keeping both senses at once is the hard part.
'A pecorone' comes from pecora, 'sheep', and carries an earthy, even crude posture. Almost every sample flattens it to 'on all fours'.

clusters.gloss: on all fours / hands and knees
on all fours like sheep (etymology kept)

lines.note: 'Dio benedetto' is both a reverent title and an everyday exclamation ('God bless him!'). The sonnet's irreverence turns on the two senses together.

clusters.gloss: who splits them in two, white and black

lines.note: Belli's speaker maps hell and heaven onto a Roman house: cellar and roof. Almost all samples keep the domestic joke; one abstracts it away.

clusters.gloss: one to the cellar, one to the roof (domestic)

lines.note: A 'sonagliera' is a harness of bells for a horse: the angels as a jingling carriage team. Most samples keep the sound but lose the object.

clusters.gloss: a jingling troop / crowd (sound kept, object lost)
of angels, as if going to bed

lines.note: 'E bbona sera' is both 'good night' and 'and that's the end of it'. The universe ends with a shrug. This is the biggest interpretive fork in the poem.
